$comment: Copy this file to the repository root as semantic-oracles.json. For every automated requirement, name an independently reviewed black-box/property test under tests/semantic-oracles/. Do not point at the ordinary implementation unit test.

oracles.purpose: Given a new user and empty storage, when they complete the primary journey using only the documented interface, then the outcome named in the brief exists and is readable on a second visit.
Given a database at the previous schema version with representative rows, when the migration runs, then all rows remain readable and no column required by the new code is null.
Given a subject with records in every table, when deletion runs, then a query for that subject across all tables returns zero rows.
Given valid credentials, when the user signs in, then a session is issued and the identifier is not placed in a URL.
Given a user without the required role, when the operation is attempted directly against the API, then it is refused even if the UI hides the control.
Given two tenants with records, when tenant A lists records, then no tenant B identifier appears.
Given the contract and the implementation, when the contract check runs, then they agree on paths, methods, status codes and error shape.
Given an invalid payload, when the response is inspected, then its shape matches the documented envelope and the machine code is stable across releases.
Given the same event delivered twice, when both are processed, then exactly one record exists and one side effect occurred.
Given a payment intent confirmed twice with the same idempotency key, when both requests are handled, then one charge exists.
Given a failing dependency, when a request is traced, then its log lines share one correlation ID and include the dependency name and outcome.
Given N+1 requests within the window, when the last is made, then it is refused with 429 and no state change occurred.
Given a privileged action, when it completes or fails, then exactly one audit record exists and the application user has no update or delete grant on that table.
Given a requirement anchored to a deleted test, when CI runs, then it fails and names the requirement.
Given the invariants listed in the domain model, when the suite runs, then each invariant is covered by a test that fails if its rule is inverted.
Given a request body containing a 16-digit card number, when it is processed, then it is refused and the value is absent from logs.
Given a token issued for tenant A, when tenant B presents it, then the operation is refused.
Given a change approved by its author, when CI evaluates it, then it is refused.
Given an actor who created a manual journal or adjustment, when the same actor attempts to approve it, then the application rejects the approval.
Given a closed period, when a write or edit dated inside that period is attempted, then the application rejects it and leaves prior balances unchanged.
Given a stored financial audit entry, when an update or delete is attempted, then storage rejects it and retention preserves entries younger than seven years.
Given a fault crossing configured availability or data-integrity thresholds, when detected, then a structured incident record is persisted with detection time, classification and escalation deadline.
Given a simulated dependency outage, when requests hit a critical workflow, then the application fails closed with no partial state corruption and emits a recovery metric.
Given an external provider not listed in the ICT register, when configuration is validated, then validation fails naming the unregistered provider.

Given an operation governed by the rule that when a payout exceeds 1000000 euro cents, the ledger shall require a distinct second treasury approver before posting, when executed on both compliant and violating inputs, then compliant inputs succeed and violating inputs are rejected.

Given an input or action that violates "When a settlement request reuses an idempotency key with altered parameters, the ledger shall reject the transfer with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT", when the operation is attempted, then the application rejects it with a typed error and performs no state change.
